topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, practical links, and core learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer etiology and the interplay of genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises through genetic mutations, microenvironmental factors, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures versus random chance.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and infectious carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific biological agents, dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical exposures drive oncogenesis through direct DNA damage, metabolic activation, or inflammatory tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methods for determining carcinogenicity and assessing exposure risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the genomic sequencing, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify mutagenic signatures and evaluate carcinogenic risk.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reviewing the main takeaways and closing the lecture.
